# Every built-in module

This install ships **43 node types** — the cards you can drop on a
canvas — plus providers, CLI verbs, MCP tools, agent skills, worked examples
and scaffolding templates. This page is the index: one line on each, and a
link to the page that goes deeper where one exists.

Nothing here is typed by hand. Every row is read out of the data the editor
and the compiler already use, by `scripts/build_module_index.py`, so a type
added, removed or re-described on Monday cannot leave this page telling you
otherwise on Tuesday. If you would rather have it in your terminal,
`openstategraph nodes` prints the same briefs, and `openstategraph nodes
<type>` adds that card's fields and ports.

## The node vocabulary

**43 types**, by the category the editor's palette groups them under:
inputs 3 · agent 10 · tools 22 · memory 1 · resolve 2 · output 2 · compose 1 · annotate 2.

A card is a *kind of step*. You configure one — a model, a sentence of rules, an allowlist — rather than writing a class for it; that is the whole bargain of this product. Drawing them and wiring them is [on the canvas](on-the-canvas.md); what the wires mean is [ports and edges](ports-and-edges.md).

### Inputs — where a run starts (3)

Every flow begins with something the run is *given*. These three are that something: a prompt typed into the box, a Markdown file of instructions, or a named rules layer you reuse across workflows. They call no model and cost nothing; they just hand the first words to whatever is wired after them.

| Type | Name | What it does | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input.markdown` | Markdown File | A Markdown instruction file for the agent. | [on the canvas](on-the-canvas.md) |
| `input.skill` | Skill | A named rules layer, written from a standard template. | [skills](the-openstategraph-skill.md) |
| `input.text` | Text Input | The starting prompt for the flow. | [on the canvas](on-the-canvas.md) |

### Agents and control flow — what decides (10)

This is where the thinking and the branching live. An **AI Agent** is one model with tools attached. The rest are the shapes you build *around* it: a router that picks a branch, a grader that sends weak work back with feedback, an orchestrator that splits a job across workers, a guard that refuses, a human who approves. Several of them call no model at all — they run a function you wrote and take the branch it names, which is cheaper and repeatable.

| Type | Name | What it does | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `agent.llm` | AI Agent | Runs an LLM with tool calling. | [on the canvas](on-the-canvas.md) |
| `function.format_report` | Format Report | Joins worker results into one Markdown report. | [on the canvas](on-the-canvas.md) |
| `guard.check` | Guard | Runs a package function against the candidate and routes pass/revise. No model. | [guard patterns](patterns.md) |
| `guard.policy` | Guardrail | Applies a PII policy to whatever passes through, and refuses what it must. | [guard patterns](patterns.md) |
| `human.approval` | Human approval | Pauses the run and waits for a person to approve or reject the candidate. | [approval in the loop](patterns.md) |
| `orchestrate.supervisor` | Orchestrator | Splits an instruction into subtasks and fans them out to workers. | [orchestrator/worker](patterns.md) |
| `orchestrate.worker` | Worker | Runs one subtask dispatched by an orchestrator. | [orchestrator/worker](patterns.md) |
| `route.check` | Check router | Runs a package function against the candidate and takes the branch it names. No model. | [routing patterns](patterns.md) |
| `route.classifier` | Router | Classifies the input and sends it down one branch — or, in parallel, down every branch that matches. | [routing patterns](patterns.md) |
| `route.grader` | Grader | Checks an answer, and sends it back with feedback if it falls short. | [grading](evaluation.md) |

### Tools — what an agent can reach for (22)

A tool is a capability you plug into an agent's `tools` bus; the agent decides when to call it. Nothing here runs on its own. They are the largest family because they are the one you extend most: the database readers, the web readers, the platform's own introspection, and `MCP server`, which brings in every tool some other service already publishes. Writing your own is [building an atom](building-an-atom.md).

| Type | Name | What it does | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tool.chinook-execute-sql` † | Execute SQL Query | Executes a SQL SELECT query against the Chinook database and returns results. | [declaring a table](declaring-a-table.md) |
| `tool.chinook-get-all-tables` † | List All Tables | Returns every table in the Chinook database, with row counts. | [declaring a table](declaring-a-table.md) |
| `tool.chinook-get-schema` † | Get Table Schema | Retrieves the schema (columns, types and foreign keys) of whichever Chinook table the agent asks about. | [declaring a table](declaring-a-table.md) |
| `tool.databricks-query` | Run Databricks Query | Runs one read-only SELECT against a Databricks SQL warehouse and returns the rows as a table. Only tables the allowlist pinned may be named. | [declaring a table](declaring-a-table.md) |
| `tool.email-send` | Email Send | Sends a report to the address configured here — the model writes subject and body, never the recipient. Dry-run (.eml to workflows/_outbox) unless SMTP is configured. | [building a tool](building-an-atom.md) |
| `tool.knowledge-lookup` | Knowledge | The workflow’s second brain: agents look up per-topic procedural knowledge (table meanings, column semantics, JOIN rules) on demand — never stuffed into the prompt. “Build second brain” on the card writes the docs at build time; a run only ever reads them. The lookup binds to every agent in the package automatically whenever knowledge/ is non-empty — this card is where you see and build the docs, not what connects them. | [the second brain](second-brain.md) |
| `tool.mcp` | MCP server | Binds every tool a Model Context Protocol server offers onto an agent — the LangChain docs, an internal service, anything that speaks MCP over HTTP. | [the MCP layer](mcp.md) |
| `tool.mssql-query` | Run T-SQL Query | Runs one read-only T-SQL SELECT against an MSSQL database and returns the rows as a table. Only tables the allowlist pinned may be named. | [declaring a table](declaring-a-table.md) |
| `tool.platform-describe-workflow` | Describe Workflow | One workflow’s docs and structure (read-only). | [the MCP layer](mcp.md) |
| `tool.platform-grep` | Repo Grep | Searches repository text (read-only, jailed, capped). | [the MCP layer](mcp.md) |
| `tool.platform-list-workflows` | List Workflows | Lists every workflow on this platform (read-only). | [the MCP layer](mcp.md) |
| `tool.platform-ls` | Repo ls | Lists a repository directory (read-only, jailed). | [the MCP layer](mcp.md) |
| `tool.platform-read-file` | Repo Read File | Reads one repository text file (read-only, jailed, capped). | [the MCP layer](mcp.md) |
| `tool.reddit-search` | Search Reddit | Finds trending posts in a subreddit. | [building a tool](building-an-atom.md) |
| `tool.session-identity` | Session Identity | Who the run belongs to — the user, the session and the thread id. Read-only, and taken from the run rather than from anything said in it. | [building a tool](building-an-atom.md) |
| `tool.sql-get-schema` | Get Schema | Columns, types and foreign keys for one table in the configured SQL database. | [declaring a table](declaring-a-table.md) |
| `tool.sql-list-tables` | List Tables | Every table in the configured SQL database, with row counts. Orientation first — an agent calls this before it knows what exists. | [declaring a table](declaring-a-table.md) |
| `tool.sql-query` | Run Query | Runs one read-only SELECT against the configured SQL database and returns the rows as a table. | [declaring a table](declaring-a-table.md) |
| `tool.validate-workflow` | Validate Workflow | Compile-checks a workflow document an agent has composed: entry points, routes, tool bindings, warnings and unknown node types. Plans a graph in memory and throws it away — nothing is saved or run. | [the MCP layer](mcp.md) |
| `tool.web-fetch` | Web Fetch | Reads one public web page as text (SSRF-guarded). | [building a tool](building-an-atom.md) |
| `tool.web-search` | Web Search | Keyless web search (DuckDuckGo); pair with Web Fetch. | [building a tool](building-an-atom.md) |
| `tool.youtube-transcript` | YouTube Transcript | Reads one YouTube video’s captions as plain text (keyless, no timestamps). | [building a tool](building-an-atom.md) |

### Memory — what survives a step (1)

One card, and it is about *carrying* rather than *storing*: whatever crosses it is recorded, and the segment's earlier entries are handed to whatever comes next. Per-topic knowledge an agent looks things up in is a tool, not this — see `Knowledge` in the tools table.

| Type | Name | What it does | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `memory.segment` | Memory segment | Records what crosses it, and hands the segment’s earlier entries to whatever comes next. | [on the canvas](on-the-canvas.md) |

### Resolve — deciding before the model does (2)

Two cards that answer a question *before* a model gets to guess at it: which store should answer this, and what do this domain's words mean. Both report what they covered as well as what they found, and neither makes a model call — which is exactly why they exist. A model asked to pick a source will always pick one.

| Type | Name | What it does | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resolve.source` | Resolve source | Names which of the stores that could answer this question is answering it, before the model picks, and lists the alternatives it did not take. No model call. | [the second brain](second-brain.md) |
| `resolve.vocabulary` | Resolve vocabulary | Looks up what the question’s words mean in this domain before the model runs, and reports what it covered as well as what it found. No model call. | [the second brain](second-brain.md) |

### Output — what a run says (2)

How a finished run presents itself: rendered as Markdown, or a fixed sentence you wrote for a branch that has to say something without spending a model call on it.

| Type | Name | What it does | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `output.formatted` | Formatted Output | Renders the result as Markdown. | [on the canvas](on-the-canvas.md) |
| `output.static` | Static Output | Prints a sentence you write — for a branch that must say something. | [on the canvas](on-the-canvas.md) |

### Compose — a workflow inside a workflow (1)

One card, and the reason workflows scale past one canvas: another workflow, mounted as a single step. Task in, answer out. It is mounted **by reference** — change the original and every mount of it changes — which is what separates a *package* from a *template*.

| Type | Name | What it does | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workflow.subgraph` | Workflow | Another workflow, run as one isolated step — task in, answer out. It brings its own state, tools and knowledge, and by reference: change the original and every mount of it changes. | [mounts and portability](export-and-portability.md) |

### Annotate — for the humans reading the canvas (2)

Neither of these compiles to anything. They are the labels and frames that make a canvas readable six months later.

| Type | Name | What it does | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `annotate.group` | Group | Frames related nodes together. | [on the canvas](on-the-canvas.md) |
| `annotate.note` | Note | A Markdown note on the canvas. | [on the canvas](on-the-canvas.md) |

† **Workflow-scoped** — 3 of the 43 (`tool.chinook-execute-sql`, `tool.chinook-get-all-tables`, `tool.chinook-get-schema`) are contributed by a workflow
package rather than by the install, so they appear only in a project that
carries that package. Your own `tools/*.py` become cards the same way — see
[building an atom](building-an-atom.md).

## When this page is wrong

It cannot be, quietly. `backend/tests/test_documented_modules_match_the_vocabulary.py`
renders the page afresh and compares it byte for byte, so a type with no row,
a row with no type, and a description that has moved are all one red test.
Regenerate with:

```bash
python3 scripts/build_module_index.py --write
```
